title: GovEagle adds document silencing to the Content Library
summary: Silence a Content Library document and GovEagle stops using it in searches and answers. Anyone can still open it, and you can @ mention it in a chat.
body_markdown:
You can now silence a document in the Content Library, so GovEagle stops using it in searches and answers without you deleting it.


## What changed


Some files belong in your Content Library but shouldn't shape every answer, such as an outdated capability statement or a proposal you lost. Now:


- **Skipped by search.** GovEagle stops pulling a silenced document into searches and answers, for everyone in your organization.
- **Still there for people.** Anyone can still open the document, download it and organize it.
- **Available when you ask.** @ mention a silenced document whenever you want it in a chat. GovEagle uses it in that chat only, and it stays silenced everywhere else.
- **Easy to spot.** Silenced documents appear dimmed with an indicator, in the Content Library and in the Office add-ins.
- **Reversible.** Unsilence a document at any time to make it searchable again.


## Who it helps


Proposal and knowledge managers who keep old versions and lost bids for reference but don't want them reused in new drafts.


## How silencing works


1. In the Content Library, click the **⋯** menu on the document's row and choose **Silence** .
2. To use the document in one chat, @ mention it or attach it.
3. To reverse it, choose **Unsilence** from the same menu.


Get GovCon capture and proposal insights in your inbox.


## Where it fits


Silencing is part of[GovEagle's Content Library](https://www.goveagle.com/solutions/knowledge-management) .


## What it doesn't do


- **Documents only, not folders.** Silence each file on its own.
- **It needs write permission.** Only users with write permissions on a document can silence it.
- **It isn't access control.** Silencing changes what GovEagle's search uses, not who can see the file.
